resources.string: See what your apps send, and to whom. Then stop it.
Hardware check, signed with Google\'s attestation key: the bootloader is locked and the system is verified.
The hardware check is not available on this phone.
Show only apps that need attention
VPN app that can control the phone

This VPN app also holds access that lets it read the screen or notifications, or control the phone, and your traffic already passes through it. Unless you know why it needs this, revoke the access or uninstall the app.
Can read the screen or control the phone
This app can read what is on the screen or in your notifications, or manage the device. Keep this only for apps you fully trust.
The phone maker preinstalled this app from %1$s, a company whose business is collecting data. It runs even if you never use it. You can disable it in system settings.
This app may install other apps. Malware spreads this way. Allow it only for app stores you trust.
This app may use the microphone, the camera or your location while you use it. Check whether it really needs this.
This app contains code from companies that collect data about how it is used, for advertising, analytics or profiling. Each one is listed on this page.
This app\'s code could not be read, so it was not checked for trackers.
The app\'s code refers to these trackers but does not contain their code.
Tracker signatures: εxodus tracker database, available under the Open Database License (ODbL).
Not from a known app store
This app was not installed from a known app store. That is fine if you installed it yourself from its official website; a modified copy can carry spyware.
A certificate authority was added to this phone. Whoever controls it can read encrypted traffic, for example a VPN provider or an employer. Remove it unless you know exactly why it is there.
Devices on the same network can try to connect to this phone and control it. Turn it off when you are not developing apps.
The bootloader is unlocked, so the system can be replaced without your knowledge. If you did not unlock it yourself, treat this as a serious warning.
The bootloader reports that the operating system could not be verified with the maker\'s key.
A computer connected by cable can install apps and read data once you accept its key. Turn it off when you do not need it.
The last security patch on this phone is more than a year old, so known vulnerabilities are not fixed.
This phone attests only in software, so hardware cannot confirm the system state. This is normal for emulators.
Google has revoked a key in this phone\'s hardware check, for example because it leaked. The bootloader and system state that the check reports may be forged.

This phone\'s hardware check is not signed with Google\'s attestation key, so the bootloader and system state that it reports cannot be confirmed. Some makers outside Google\'s programme use their own key; a modified system can also cause this.
All traffic currently passes through a VPN app. Make sure it is one you trust.
Apps that can use them: %1$d. Review each one and allow only what it needs.

Android does not let one app change another app\'s permissions, so this review guides you through them. For each app, open its permissions and choose to be asked every time, or deny the access. Reviewed apps are ticked; if one gains access again, it comes back here.

This voice assistant can keep the microphone open to listen for its wake word. On a test phone, the Google app did so around the clock until “Hey Google” was turned off. Turn it off unless you use it.

1. Open the app in system settings.\n2. Tap Disable or Turn off.\n3. If the button is greyed out, the phone maker blocks it. From a computer with USB debugging, you can remove the app for your user instead; this can be undone.
Datapavan compares your apps and your phone with these databases. All of them are on the phone; nothing is looked up online.
Data pack %1$d of %2$s, included with the app.
Google key attestation roots and revocation list

Datapavan never goes online. A newer data pack can come from the project\'s release page, from a mirror or from another phone. It must be signed by the project: Datapavan checks the signature before it reads anything, and refuses a pack that is not newer than the one in use.
This build trusts no data-signing key yet, so it cannot import packs.
Data pack %1$d is now in use.
This file is not a signed Datapavan data pack.
This pack is signed by a key that Datapavan does not trust.
The signature does not match: the file was changed or damaged.
This pack needs a newer version of Datapavan.
This file is too large to be a data pack.
This pack is not newer than the one in use.
The file could not be read.
Fingerprint (SHA-256), to compare with the one published with the pack:
This data is from %1$s, more than six months ago. Tracker lists and security data change; import a newer data pack.
This copy is not signed by its developer. Someone changed it, and a modified VPN or proxy app can read everything that passes through it.
Datapavan knows this app, but not yet the key of the channel this copy came from. That is common for copies from app stores and is not a warning.
Genuine copy of %1$s, signed by its developer.
Genuine copy of %1$s, signed by Google Play for its developer.
Genuine copy of %1$s, built and signed by F-Droid.
It is signed with an earlier key of the developer, which the app has since replaced.
Datapavan knows %1$s, but not yet the key of this copy. Copies from app stores often carry the store\'s key. Compare this fingerprint with the one the developer publishes:
This copy of %1$s is not signed by its developer. Someone changed it, and it can see everything that passes through it. Remove it and install %1$s from its official website or store.
This copy of %1$s carries a debug key, which the developer\'s own builds never use: someone else rebuilt it. Remove it and install %1$s from its official website or store.
Signed with the key of a known app. Show which
A genuine build of %1$s under another name. Its developer disguises some builds to protect people whose phones are searched.
Official signing certificates of VPN, proxy and circumvention apps
This app contains code that can let other people\'s internet traffic pass through this phone. Details are on this page.
This app contains code that lets a support agent see the screen and, in some cases, control the phone. Details are on this page.
Records your use of this app
This app contains code that can record what you see and tap in it, so that its maker can replay it.
Connection sharing, remote support and recording

Its maker describes it as a way for apps to earn money by letting the maker\'s customers send internet traffic through their users\' phones. When this code is on, other people\'s traffic passes through your phone: websites see it as coming from your internet connection, and it uses your data and battery.
Datapavan found the code, not its activity. It cannot tell whether this feature is on in this app, or whether you agreed to it.
%1$s says the code stays off until the user agrees in the app, and that the app must let you turn it off at any time.
In this app\'s settings, look for a switch called “%1$s”.
Google Play allows apps to carry traffic for others only when that is the app\'s main, visible purpose.
A remote support tool. Depending on how this app uses it, it can:
show a support agent this app\'s screen
show a support agent your whole screen, including other apps and the keyboard
let the agent tap and type in this app, if you allow it
let the agent control your phone, including other apps and settings, once its accessibility service is turned on
This app\'s accessibility service is turned on, so this tool can control apps other than this one.
Finding the code does not show that anyone has connected to your phone.
It can record what you see and tap in this app and send it to %1$s, so that the app\'s maker can replay it. It records this app only, not other apps.
The app\'s maker can also watch a session while it is happening.
Datapavan cannot tell whether recording is on.
Identified on %1$s in the SDK that %2$s publishes.
SDKs that share the connection, give remote support or record the screen
